summary: 100-foot steel tower (Aermotor per one source) in St. Croix State Park, Pine County, MN; built 1936 or 1937 by the CCC, staffed until 1981, listed as standing and open to climb.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with cross-bracing; Aermotor maker per one source (Forest Lookouts)

access.note: Open to park visitors to climb; the state's fire towers are usually open but closed November 1 through May 31, per a Savage Pacer column

events.note: Forest Lookouts and a Savage Pacer column say 1936; the NRHP nomination gives 1936-37; the DNR page and Wikipedia say 1937
Newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts names a woman employed at the fire tower
Staffing ended when aerial surveys became the standard

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination gives 1936-37, which covers both years. The single-year sources still differ (1936 in Forest Lookouts and the Savage Pacer column; 1937 in the DNR page and Wikipedia), so the story reports both.

sources.title: St. Croix State Park CCC/WPA/Rustic Style Historic Resources (National Register nomination)
Commentary: Fire towers provide a different view of Minnesota

notes_for_editor: Aermotor rests on one source (Forest Lookouts); the NRHP calls it a standard 100-foot steel tower and does not name a maker. Build year is disputed (1936 vs 1937). The seasonal closure comes from a guest column, not a DNR notice, so confirm current park hours before relying on it. The 1948 item is quoted by Forest Lookouts and was not checked against the newspaper. The 'record' 1936 build year is supported by two sources but not the DNR page. Wikidata (inception 1930s) was not used.
